newsitem.title: KENYA: Rwandan party condemns "conspiracy against Hutus".
newsitem.headline: Rwandan party condemns "conspiracy against Hutus".

text.p: The Rwandan opposition RDR party on Sunday accused Rwanda and its neighbours of a conspiracy against Hutu refugees and specifically condemned Tanzania for driving ethnic Hutu refugees back home "at gun point".

In a statement issued in the Kenyan capital of Nairobi, Rally for the Return of Democracy in Rwanda (RDR) complained of anti-Hutu refugee sentiment in Rwanda and Uganda and a lack of concern among Rwanda's neighbours and the international community.

"The Tanzanian government decision to forcefully repatriate Rwandan refugees in what is seen as an international conspiracy against Hutu refugees is a departure from all existing legal provisions," said RDR, a mainly Hutu party.
The Tanzanian army drove an estimated 200,000 refugees from the largest refugee camp in Tanzania at the weekend and herded people to the nearby Rusomo border crossing into Rwanda.

The refugees have resisted returning to Rwanda, usually because they fear retribution for the 1994 massacre in Rwanda of some 800,000 Tutsis by Hutu militia. Many Hutus -- some associated with the killings -- fled the country after Tutsi rebels took over the government.
The exodus followed talks between camp leaders in Benaco and officials of the Tanzanian government, which says it wants all 540,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees in Tanzania out by December 31.

The latest migration was the second mass return of Rwandan refugees. More than 500,000 left Zaire in four days from November 15 after a rebellion by Zairean Tutsis broke the hold of Hutus trying to stop others from returning.
